headline: Markets Cap a Winning Week as Healthcare and Software Lead Friday's Advance
body_html:
Equity markets finished the week on a constructive note Friday, October 9, with 344 stocks rising against 196 falling across our 544-name universe. Healthcare topped the sector leaderboard, gaining 1.45%, while Software added 1.04%. Telehealth name Hims & Hers Health surged 10.19% to pace all gainers, followed by cybersecurity firm Zscaler up 7.80% and data-cloud platform Snowflake up 7.42%. Observability software provider Datadog rose 7.11%, reinforcing a broad bid for enterprise software names heading into the weekend.

Not every corner of the market fared well. Homebuilders slid 1.44% and Semiconductors dipped 0.48%, dragged in part by Cirrus Logic and Skyworks Solutions, which fell 5.59% and 5.45% respectively. Real-estate brokerage eXp World Holdings was Friday's sharpest decliner, off 7.23%, while Fair Isaac dropped 5.63% in the financial-data space. Consumer names were effectively flat on the day, up just 0.03% as a group.

Wall Street enters the new week with earnings season revving up and fresh inflation data on the docket — a combination that kept the broader market on track for weekly gains. Geopolitical attention also sharpens after a deadly blast at Riyadh's airport, though major Saudi conferences are reported to be proceeding. Traders will look to Monday, October 12, to set the early tone for what promises to be a data-heavy stretch.

briefs.headline: Earnings and Inflation Data Set to Drive the Week Ahead
briefs.body: Investors return Monday with two powerful catalysts in view: the first wave of third-quarter corporate earnings reports and a closely watched inflation reading. Analysts expect the combination to test recent gains, particularly in rate-sensitive sectors that have been trading near multi-week highs.

briefs.headline: Riyadh Airport Blast Puts Gulf Risk Back on the Radar
briefs.body: An explosion at Riyadh's airport wounded multiple people, according to eyewitness accounts reported by Reuters. Organizers of major upcoming Saudi business conferences said events would proceed as planned despite the incident, though the attack is likely to keep geopolitical risk premium elevated in energy markets at the open.

briefs.headline: Trump-Putin Call Cools Ukraine Ceasefire Hopes
briefs.body: The Kremlin indicated that a phone conversation between President Trump and Russian President Putin produced little momentum toward resuming Ukraine peace negotiations in the near term. The signal adds uncertainty to any diplomatic timeline and may weigh on European defense and energy sentiment early in the week.

briefs.headline: Tech Volatility Remains a Live Theme After Whipsaw Week
briefs.body: Last week's AI-driven equity trade delivered both record highs and sharp intraday reversals, underscoring how quickly sentiment can shift in growth-technology names. Friday's strong showings from cloud and cybersecurity stocks suggest some stabilization, but traders will watch whether that momentum carries into Monday's session.

briefs.headline: Supreme Court Weighs Case That Could Reshape Retirement-Plan Investing
briefs.body: Justices are signaling varying positions in a significant 401(k) case examining whether plan sponsors can include private-market funds and whether underperformance creates legal liability. A ruling favorable to plaintiffs could force widespread reassessment of target-date and alternative-investment allocations inside defined-contribution plans.

briefs.headline: Fed Governance Spotlight Intensifies Around Lisa Cook Committee
briefs.body: A newly formed committee tasked with reviewing Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook's appointment is drawing scrutiny over its scope and authority. The inquiry adds another layer of institutional uncertainty around Fed independence at a moment when markets are already parsing every signal on the interest-rate path.
